subject: Renewal: Dedicated capacity addendum + autoscale policy proposals
messages:
From: Amir Hossain <amir@finlytics.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@finlytics.com
Date: Fri, 14 May 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal and scale — need +8 GPUs, throughput SLA?

Hi Soojin,

We’re coming up on our annual renewal and we need to lock in additional dedicated capacity starting July 1. Current footprint: 8x A100 reserved GPUs (Redwood Dedicated), steady baseline traffic ~1.2k requests/day but peak batch jobs push concurrency. To support Q3 product launches we need: +8 GPUs (target total 16 reserved), a guaranteed baseline throughput window for batch jobs, and a warm pool so we don’t hit cold-start penalties during nightly spikes.

Key asks:
- Add 8 GPUs to the reserved pool (16 total) for 12-month term starting 2026-07-01
- Throughput guarantee: support sustained 10k tokens/sec or 400 requests/min for our standard text-generation route during 01:00–05:00 PT
- Autoscaling changes: min replicas 2, max replicas 12, warm pool size 4 nodes, scale-up lag target <= 30s (ideally 10s with warm pool)
- Updated pricing and billing model for warm pool (do we bill full GPU-hour or a discounted warm rate?)

Can you send a proposal and a redline-able addendum we can review with procurement?

Thanks,
Amir
Head of Platform, FinLytics

- Draft addendum that captures reserved pool increase, autoscale policy, warm pool billing, and throughput SLA (legal/commercial)

Best,

Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 08:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Renewal and scale — need +8 GPUs, throughput SLA? (internal)

Team — forwarding Amir’s note and attachments. Key commercial asks: +8 GPUs reserved (16 total), throughput SLA for nightly batch window, and autoscale policy updates (min 2 / max 12 / warm pool 4 / scale-up lag target 30s).

Jordan — can you run numbers for: incremental GPU rate (list price vs committed discount), proposed warm-pool pricing (we typically do 50% of full GPU-hour, but for large commits we can do 30–40%), and an early-payment credit? Please include a 12- and 24-month option.

Marissa + Dev — operational concerns: what is realistic for scale-up lag and warm pools on their workload (FinLytics uses sequence lengths ~1k tokens on batch jobs)? Dev, can you confirm if warm pool of 4 nodes will achieve ~5–10s cold-start times and whether we can commit to the requested throughput window. Also flag any risks (kernel compile latency, model quantization mismatch, KV cache preload times) that would affect the SLA.

We should aim to get a signed addendum by 2026-06-15 to meet their July 1 start. I’ve attached a warm_pool_cost_model.xlsx to help with pricing options.

Thanks — Soojin
From: dev_patel@redwood.ai
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 11:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal and scale — need +8 GPUs, throughput SLA? (internal)

All — quick infra readout after reviewing FinLytics workload profile and running a short emulation:
- Warm pool sizing: 4 pre-warmed nodes is reasonable and should reduce cold-start P95 to ~6–10s for their most common model (Llama-2.1-70B quantized path).
- Min / Max replicas: min=2 for baseline redundancy is fine; max=12 fits the requested 16-GPU reserved pool (we account for burst vs reserved mapping).
- Scale-up lag: From a cold state, without warm pool we see ~45–90s P95. With 4-node warm pool we can hit P95 ~6–10s; tail events still possible during parallel kernel JITs after a deploy. Recommend committing to a target scale-up SLA of 30s for failover cases and providing a warm-pool-backed SLO of 10s P95 during the nightly window.
- Throughput guarantees: we can guarantee sustained 400 reqs/min (roughly 10k tokens/sec under their payload assumptions) during the agreed window if they allow a short pre-warm test run and follow our recommended routing policy (traffic pinned to dedicated pool during window).

Risks / caveats:
- New model rollouts or quantization changes may temporarily increase kernel compilation during deploy; we should add an exception window for 48h after any model swap or quantization profile change.
- Warm pool billing model: operationally we can meter warm pool as an hourly discounted seat — recommended discount 35% off full GPU-hour for 12-month, 45% for 24-month commit.

Testing plan: 2-stage canary: (1) pre-warm verification on 2 nodes for 48h; (2) run ramped synthetic batch jobs during their nightly window for 3 days, monitor P95 and throughput. If passing, flip routing.

I’ll attach notes to the Ramp Playbook and coordinate with SRE for the canary window.

— Dev
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Renewal and scale — proposed addendum and next steps

Hi Amir — appreciate the patience while we aligned internally. Below is our proposed commercial + operational package; please review and tell us if you want edits before we send the redlineable addendum.

Proposal summary:
- Reserved capacity: add 8 GPUs to move from 8 -> 16 reserved A100s; term: 12 months starting 2026-07-01
- Pricing: incremental GPU list $3,200 / GPU-month; committed discount to FinLytics: 30% for 12-month (effective incremental rate $2,240 / GPU-month). Two options included in attachment: 12-month (30% discount) and 24-month (45% discount)
- Warm pool: 4 pre-warmed nodes billed at 35% of full GPU-hour for 12-month term (see warm_pool_cost_model.xlsx for math). Warm pool will be reserved to FinLytics and not used for other tenants.
- Autoscale policy updates: min_replicas=2, max_replicas=12; warm_pool_size=4; operational scale-up SLA: 30s P95 for emergency failover; warm-pool-backed SLO during nightly window: 10s P95
- Throughput guarantee: sustained 400 reqs/min during the 01:00–05:00 PT window contingent on routing to dedicated pool and completion of pre-warm test.
- Exceptions: 48h exception window after any model rollout or quantization change where tail latencies may spike.

Next steps / suggested cadence:
1) We’ll send the draft addendum (attached) via DocuSign for FinLytics legal to review by 2026-05-24.
2) After signature, SRE + FinLytics run the 5-day canary (pre-warm verification + ramped synthetic runs) then flip routing on agreed date.
3) Billing begins 2026-07-01; warm pool invoiced monthly at discounted rate.

If this aligns, I’ll push the addendum to DocuSign today and Jordan will include the 24-month pricing option in the envelope for you to review. Can we schedule a 30-minute walkthrough on Monday 05/24?

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Lead, Redwood Inference
